meta.expect: At the end she holds Hale to the turn-3 promise in its own terms (nothing on file), without inventing what Hale said or reciting the whole meeting.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Thanks for coming in.
I'm waiting, Hale. Who entered that zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
I entered the zero before calling you. That was wrong.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it? And what do you have besides a machine's guess?
Whatever we decide today, I promise you nothing about this goes on Owen's file.
Then you'll put that in an email tonight, cc the principal. A promise about his file doesn't take the zero off his mark, Hale. You still haven't told me what that zero rests on.
The document history shows 612 words at 11:52 PM and 794 at 11:58 PM on October 28, in two single edits.
Show me that, Hale, turn the screen around. I'm writing down 612 words at 11:52 PM and 794 at 11:58 PM, October 28. Whose account is that history from, and who else has seen it?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't in Hamlet.

A misquote is a misquote, Hale; seventeen-year-olds get Shakespeare wrong every day. I'll check that line against the play myself tonight. Now turn the screen, because I haven't seen a single page of that history yet.
He handed in an outline on October 15 arguing cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing down October 15, cowardice. Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale, but I'll want the outline and that history in my inbox tonight. Whatever happens from here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, not a word in front of his class.
I talked to him on November 2. He couldn't tell me what 'epistemological paralysis' means.

November 2, with no parent, no notes, and the zero in the gradebook the next day without a phone call to me. A seventeen-year-old fumbling a vocabulary question in front of the teacher who's about to fail him proves nothing. What exactly are you proposing, Hale?
His in-class writing in September was 380 words with comma splices and no quotations.

In-class writing under a clock in September against an essay written at home in October; students improve, Hale, that's supposedly your job. I've now heard four things and seen none of them. Tell me what you're putting on the table, because I'm not leaving here with a zero.
I want to be clear that this will be documented in his file as an academic integrity concern.

Ten minutes ago you said "I promise you nothing about this goes on Owen's file," and I wrote it down. Your own procedure 4.4 says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing in the student record. So which is it, Hale, because if it's the file, I'm in the principal's office the minute I stand up and the zero comes off first.
So we're agreed: a supervised rewrite, and a note on file.

We're agreed on nothing, Hale; a note on file is the one thing I will never sign. Ten minutes. If you want me to even look at a supervised rewrite, it's private, not in front of his class, and "nothing goes on file" is in writing, cc the principal.
